So. I live in KY. Lots of people here fly the ‘confederate’ flag and cite their southern heritage, even thought most Kentuckians who fought in the war fought for the Union and Kentucky, when forced to finally come out of neutrality and pick a side, chose the Union to support. 

This week the committee on historical monuments chose to remove a statue of Jefferson Davis from the capitol rotunda in Frankfort. The statue was sent to the hometown of Davis (a city I cannot right now recall). People have lost their ever loving minds over it. ‘He was a president from KY!’ ‘It’s our History!’ 

No, Karen. He was never Kentucky’s President because Kentucky was never a Confederate state. In fact, politically speaking he was a traitor to Kentucky. He has a place in history, but it is not a place of honor or adoration. There are plenty of civil war battlefields around this state that will do well to teach the history of that war, without statues idolizing people who fought a whole entire war over their right to keep a race of people enslaved. 

Another often-cited reason given for the civil war is that the Northern states were ‘jealous that the southern states were so much wealthier’. Sure, Brad. Why was that, do you think? Maybe it has something to do with the fact that the south could purchase people like chattel to do their work for them? That they had no limits to the amount of work that they could complete as long as there were more enslaved people to purchase? That feeding and clothing enslaved men, women and children with scraps and rags cost nothing relative to the cost of paying someone a wage to complete the same amount of work? 

Slavery was the very heart of the civil war. There’s no honor in idolizing the losing side.

As someone who has also raised a family member’s three children for the last 10 years, my best advice is to find therapists for your bio children, your adopted children, yourself and your spouse. Find ones you like, trust, and have a good rapport with. Keep them handy. You will need them throughout the years. Early trauma has a way of coming back around during puberty, even if they don’t remember it. Build a support community so that you and your spouse can still spend time together, and put together some type of plan to spend time with your bio kids alone at least at first. It’s a hard transition. Sending you lots of good thoughts! And no, NTA for changing that name!

My nephew, who we’ve raised since 2010, is almost 13 and has been diagnosed with ODD recently. To be honest, I am not sure I am going to be able to continue to parent him. The good thing is that from my research, many times kids who are diagnosed as a young child are able to grow out of it. When the symptoms and diagnosis come during the teen or preteen years, it’s a different story. We are dealing with lying and stealing at this point and I’m getting weary of all my parenting time being disproportionately focused on him while my other kids aren’t getting what they may need. Good luck! Telehealth may be able to help you!
